question: Horizon Europe: case-by-case assessment versus general suspension of payments to Russian entities between 4 March and 8 April 2022

On 4 March 2022, the Commission publicly announced a general suspension of payments to, and cooperation with, Russian entities under Horizon Europe1. On 8 April 2022, the Commission announced that with the adoption of the fifth package of sanctions against Russia, the participation of all Russian public bodies or public-related entities in ongoing Horizon Europe projects would be terminated2.
In February 2026, the Commission instead stated that both the suspension of payments and the termination of participation had been carried out based on a ‘case-by-case assessment’3. 1.

How does the Commission reconcile its announcement of 4 March 2022 of a general suspension of payments to Russian beneficiaries with its claim of February 2026 that suspension decisions had been taken only subsequently under specific legal instruments as a series of individual case-by-case measures?
If there was a general suspension, what legal basis did the Commission use to enact it before the restrictive measures included the fifth package of sanctions entered into force?
If the measures were taken on a case-by-case basis, can the Commission specify how many individual decisions were taken between 4 March and 8 April 2022, and on what legal basis?
